title: Anthem RPM, CCM & RTM Rates in California | Fuse
summary: Anthem Blue Cross's negotiated California rates for remote patient monitoring, chronic care management and RTM CPT codes, from current MRF data.
body_markdown:
Remote patient monitoring (RPM), chronic care management (CCM) and remote therapeutic monitoring (RTM) are recurring, per-month revenue lines, which makes the negotiated rate behind each CPT code matter more than it does for a one-off visit: a small per-claim difference compounds across every enrolled patient, every month. Yet Anthem publishes its California negotiated rates through CMS-mandated Machine Readable Files organized by employer EIN for group plans and by HIOS number for individual plans, not as a single statewide list a practice can search. The “Anthem rate” for a given code isn’t one number, it’s whatever the aggregation across many separate employer and individual filings happens to average out to.


A quick note on methodology: the figures below come from Fuse’s own extraction of Anthem’s August 2026 California machine readable files. We pulled every dollar-denominated fee schedule rate attached to these CPT codes in the statewide network file (excluding percentage-of-charges entries), matched each listed NPI against the federal NPPES registry, kept only individual internal medicine and family medicine physicians, nurse practitioners and physician assistants — the clinician types that run most care-management programs — whose registered practice location is in California, and computed the statistics across distinct provider-rate pairs. This is the care-management counterpart to our earlier analysis of[Anthem’s behavioral health rates in California](https://www.fuseinsight.com/blog/cost-of-behavioral-therapy-anthem-california/) .


## Anthem’s Negotiated Rates for RPM, CCM and RTM CPT Codes

## Why One Anthem Number Represents Many Separate Filings


A statewide mean or median from Anthem’s California files pools an enormous number of distinct negotiated arrangements. Anthem organizes its files by employer EIN or HIOS number, so the aggregation choices behind any published statistic materially shape the result. Two practices billing the identical CPT code to Anthem in California can see meaningfully different reimbursement depending on the specific plan, the employer group behind it and the provider’s credential or setting.


Anthem also notes that its files represent an as-of-date snapshot subject to change before the next monthly update. That means a rate pulled today is directional information about where Anthem’s California network tends to land, not a number a practice can treat as fixed. A statewide average can provide a directional market benchmark, but it cannot predict payment for a particular plan, provider or visit.


## Billing Requirements Behind These Codes


The reimbursement rate is only half the revenue equation for care-management programs; each code carries service-time and data thresholds that determine whether a claim is billable at all.


- **RPM device supply (99454)** and the **RTM supply codes (98976, 98977, 98984)** are each billed once per 30 days, and 99454 requires the patient to transmit at least 16 days of readings in that period.
- **RPM setup (99453)** and **RTM setup (98975)** are one-time codes billed at the start of monitoring, covering device setup and patient education.
- **RPM management (99457)** requires 20 minutes of interactive care management time in a calendar month, with **99458** for each additional 20 minutes; **RTM management (98980/98981)** mirrors the same 20-minute structure.
- **CCM (99490)** requires 20 minutes of clinical staff time per calendar month directed by a physician or qualified health professional, while **99491** requires 30 minutes of the physician’s or QHP’s own time. **Complex CCM (99487/99489)** requires 60 minutes and moderate-to-high complexity medical decision making.


A practice that misses a threshold, a 15-day transmission month, an 18-minute management month, loses the claim entirely, which is why the per-code rates above should be read alongside the operational discipline each code demands.


## What This Means for Your Practice


Anthem rate tables pool many distinct EIN- and HIOS-organized plans into one statewide figure, which is exactly the kind of aggregation that makes a published average unreliable for a single patient.


The practical response is to verify current eligibility and plan-specific benefits for the scheduled CPT code before the visit, rather than reading a pooled statewide average as a patient-specific payment estimate. For recurring care-management billing the stakes are higher than for a single visit: an enrollment decision made on a wrong rate assumption repeats its error every month the patient stays in the program.


The same logic applies on the payment side. A statewide average cannot tell you whether Anthem is actually paying your practice what your contract says it should. That requires checking reimbursements against your own contracted rates, claim by claim. Fuse helps practices do exactly this: it verifies reimbursements against past claims data and places automated phone calls to payers to confirm insurance coverage, so discrepancies between what a contract promises and what actually gets paid surface before they quietly accumulate into lost revenue.
